name: Amazon
basis: each funding- or dividend-inclusive history is scaled to its own latest raw USD close

fundingForecast.displaySign: positive is earned by a perp long; negative is paid by a perp long

onchainSpot.preferenceBasis: all pages display separate CEX reported-volume and contract-backed DEX execution sections
onchainSpot.volumeSource: direct Binance, Bitget, Bybit, OKX, and Meteora venue APIs plus factory-verified PancakeSwap V3 pool-event volume indexed by DexScreener; DEX quote routes without indexed pool-event volume are excluded

cexMarkets.pair: No listed AMZN tokenized spot pair

peerMapping.justification: The block uses XYZ100 as the single primary index hedge because Amazon's dominant systematic exposure is US mega-cap growth and cloud/AI beta rather than broad value or commodity risk. Peers are all single-name equities from CORE_UNIVERSE, exclude AMZN, have positive weights, and sum to exactly 1. The weighting prioritizes economic comparability first: GOOGL and MSFT carry the largest weights because cloud plus advertising and enterprise cloud are closest to Amazon's AWS and ads engine; META and AAPL add consumer internet and mega-cap platform exposure; NVDA is included for the AI/cloud capex cycle but sized below the closest business-model peers; TSLA is kept smallest because liquidity alone does not offset weaker comparability. All displayed 24-hour perp liquidity figures are stated in USD millions, and because AMZN itself shows only 0.462 USD millions while every selected peer is more liquid, the construction can absorb the hedge without letting the most liquid but less comparable names dominate the block.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: Alphabet matches Amazon on cloud infrastructure, digital advertising, and consumer internet scale, giving it the highest economic comparability alongside Microsoft; its 24-hour perp liquidity is 2.262 USD millions, comfortably above AMZN, so it can carry a joint-largest weight.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft is the closest cloud hyperscaler comparison through Azure against AWS, with added enterprise software and AI platform exposure. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 1.386 USD millions, exactly three times AMZN at 0.462 USD millions, supporting a top peer weight.

peers.name: Meta Platforms
peers.reason: Meta Platforms is a mega-cap consumer internet and advertising name with similar growth-factor sensitivity and index co-movement to Amazon, though it lacks a large cloud arm, so it receives a slightly lower weight; its 24-hour perp liquidity is 1.343 USD millions.

peers.name: Apple
peers.reason: Apple contributes mega-cap consumer ecosystem and services exposure that overlaps Amazon's retail and subscription businesses, but with weaker cloud and logistics comparability, so it is weighted lower; its 24-hour perp liquidity is 1.422 USD millions.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is included because AI data-center demand tightly links it to Amazon's cloud capex cycle and growth-factor returns, even though its semiconductor economics are less directly comparable; its 24-hour perp liquidity is 3.384 USD millions, the deepest among the selected peers, which helps execution despite the lower economic weight.

peers.name: Tesla
peers.reason: Adds high-beta US mega-cap consumer/tech exposure, but it is the least economically comparable name in the block, so despite relatively deep 24-hour perp liquidity of 4.551 USD millions it receives the smallest weight.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: Amazon is a mega-cap Nasdaq-100 constituent whose equity risk is dominated by US large-cap growth and cloud/AI sentiment, so the Nasdaq-100 is the cleanest primary index hedge; its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 21.944 USD millions, which is deep relative to Amazon's own 0.462 USD millions.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's TradeXYZ close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: consolidated listed-options chain, verified earnings calendars, and split-adjusted price history

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with verified calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
